facts.statement: Ginsburg and Buffetaut described a third species, Euthecodon arambourgi, in 1978 from a skull found in Gebel Zelten, Libya.
facts.quote: A third species was described by Ginsburg and Buffetaut in 1978 based on a skull from Gebel Zelten, Libya, which was shorter proportioned than either of the two previously recognized forms.

facts.statement: Euthecodon was a long-snouted crocodile that lived throughout much of Africa during the Neogene, with fossils particularly common in Kenya, Ethiopia, and Libya.
facts.quote: Euthecodon is an extinct genus of long-snouted crocodile. It was common throughout much of Africa during the Neogene, with fossils being especially common in Kenya, Ethiopia, and Libya.

facts.statement: Euthecodon evolved its long snout independently of other crocodilians, suggesting a diet primarily consisting of fish.
facts.quote: Although superficially resembling that of gharials, the long snout was a trait developed independently from that of other crocodilians and suggests a diet of primarily fish.

facts.statement: Euthecodon is unique among long-snouted crocodilians for its deeply scalloped rostral margins and constrictions between teeth, giving the skull a saw-like appearance from above.
facts.quote: Euthecodon differs from any other known longirostrine crocodilian in its deeply scalloped rostral margins, each tooth sitting in its own bony sheath, separated from the next by a notable constriction of the rostrum, given the skull a saw-like appearance when viewed from above.

facts.statement: Euthecodon possessed slender, pointed, bicarinate teeth clearly adapted for eating fish.
facts.quote: The individual teeth are slender, isodont and pointed with two keels (bicarinate), clearly suited for a piscivorous diet.

facts.statement: Unlike other crocodilians, Euthecodon typically had only four premaxillary teeth, though E. arambourgi appears to be a transitional form retaining five.
facts.quote: Unlike any other crocodilians, Euthecodon typically possess only four premaxillary teeth instead of five, with Euthecodon arambourgi as an exception, seemingly representing a transitional form in the process of losing the tooth.

facts.statement: Euthecodon had a prominent ridge on the nasal bone leading to the eyes, creating a sloping forehead similar to Crocodylus checchiai.
facts.quote: The nasal bone bears a prominent ridge leading up to the eyes, giving its forehead a sloping appearance somewhat similar to that of Crocodylus checchiai.

facts.statement: Older Euthecodon individuals developed noticeable squamosal ridges or horns.
facts.quote: Older individuals are known to develop noticeable squamosal ridges or "horns".

facts.statement: Researchers debated whether the initial species described by Joleaud and Fourtau were distinct enough to be separate species.
facts.quote: Subsequent researchers debated whether the two species were distinct enough to form separate species.

facts.statement: Variations in tooth counts have led some researchers to question whether certain specimens assigned to E. brumpti represent a distinct species.
facts.quote: This difference in tooth count has led some researchers to question whether these specimens, typically assigned to E. brumpti, might actually represent their own species.

facts.statement: The genus Euthecodon was established by Fourtau in 1920.
facts.quote: authority: Fourtau, 1920

facts.statement: The genus Euthecodon includes three recognized species: E. nitriae, E. brumpti, and E. arambourgi.
facts.quote: subdivision: *Euthecodon nitriae Fourtau, 1920 Euthecodon brumpti (Joleaud, 1920) Euthecodon arambourgi Ginsburg and Buffetaut, 1978

facts.statement: Euthecodon arambourgi lived during the Burdigalian stage of the Miocene.
facts.quote: E. arambourgi is attested by both sets of remains as having lived during the Burdigalian stage of the Miocene

facts.statement: Euthecodon arambourgi was described based on remains found in the Miocene of Libya and Egypt.
facts.quote: Described based on remains from the Miocene of Libya (Gebel Zelten) and Egypt (Moghara)

facts.statement: Euthecodon brumpti was originally described from fossil material in the Omo Basin of Ethiopia dating to the Pliocene to Pleistocene.
facts.quote: Euthecodon brumpti was originally described based on fossil material collected in the Omo Basin of Villafranchian (Pliocene to Pleistocene), Ethiopia

facts.statement: Fossils of Euthecodon brumpti have been found at localities including Lothagam, Kanapoi, Longarakak, Nakoret, and Todenyang.
facts.quote: These localities include Lothagam (specifically the Nawata and Nachukui Formation), Kanapoi, Longarakak, Nakoret and Todenyang

facts.statement: A 2017 publication by Christopher Brochu suggests that many Miocene to Pliocene remains from the Turkana Basin may belong to an unnamed species rather than E. brumpti.
facts.quote: according to a 2017 publication by Christopher Brochu, much of the Miocene to Pliocene remains found in the Turkana Basin may instead belong to an as yet unnamed species

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that Euthecodon brumpti might be a junior synonym of E. nitriae.
facts.quote: He also mentions the possibility that the species is a junior synonym of E. nitriae, an idea that has also been suggested by past researchers

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Euthecodon was originally found at Wadi Natrun in Egypt.
facts.quote: The type species of Euthecodon, its fossils were originally found at Wadi Natrun in Egypt (Miocene or Pliocene)

facts.statement: Fossils tentatively referred to E. nitriae have been found in the Upper Miocene sediments of the Tunisian Ségui Formation.
facts.quote: Fossils tentatively referred to E. cf. nitriae have been found in the Upper Miocene (Tortonian) sediments of the Tunisian Ségui Formation

facts.statement: Remains of Euthecodon are known from the Miocene Beglia Formation in Tunisia, Early Miocene Rusinga Island, the Albertine Rift, Ombo in Kenya, and the Messinian to Zanclean Sahabi Formation in Libya.
facts.quote: Other remains of Euthecodon are known from the Miocene Beglia Formation (Tunisia), Early Miocene Rusinga Island (Lake Victoria), the Albertine Rift (Congo), Ombo (Kenya) and the Messinian to Zanclean Sahabi Formation (Libya)

facts.statement: Euthecodon shows a series of adaptations that are present in E. arambourgi, exaggerated in E. nitriae, and peak in E. brumpti.
facts.quote: Euthecodon shows a series of adaptations present in E. arambourgi and progressively exaggerated in E. nitriae, reaching their peak with E. brumpti

facts.statement: The eyes face more forward in later species of Euthecodon than in E. arambourgi.
facts.quote: The eyes also face more forward in later species than they do in E. arambourgi

facts.statement: Some traits in Euthecodon do not follow a direct evolutionary series and appear most prominent in the intermediate species E. nitriae.
facts.quote: The authors do, however, note that certain traits do not conform to such a direct evolutionary series, and instead appear most prominent in the intermediate E. nitriae

facts.statement: Later research shows that Euthecodon's resemblance to gavialoids is due to convergent evolution, placing it deeper within the Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: later research has repeatedly shown this to be merely be the result of convergent evolution, instead placing it much deeper within the Crocodylidae

facts.statement: Euthecodon differs from gavialids and tomistomines by having small supratemporal fossae and a relatively gradual narrowing of the rostrum.
facts.quote: Euthecodon differs from gavialids and most tomistomines in its small supratemporal fossae and the relatively gradual narrowing of the rostrum

facts.statement: Most current analyses place Euthecodon in Osteolaeminae, a family including the dwarf crocodile, Rimasuchus, Brochuchus, Voay, and the slender-snouted crocodile.
facts.quote: Most current analyses place it in Osteolaeminae, a family consisting of the extant dwarf crocodile and the extinct Rimasuchus, Brochuchus as well as possible Voay and the slender-snouted crocodile

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis identifies Mecistops as a close relative of Euthecodon.
facts.quote: Mecistops as a close relative of Euthecodon

facts.statement: Euthecodon has notably small supratemporal fossae, creating a weak insertion point for jaw musculature.
facts.quote: Euthecodon has notably small supratemporal fossae, creating only a weak insertion point for the jaw musculature

facts.statement: Despite its unique dental adaptations, Euthecodon likely had a relatively weak bite.
facts.quote: Despite this, however, Euthecodon would have likely still had a relatively weak bite

facts.statement: The piscivorous and aquatic lifestyle of Euthecodon was perfected in E. brumpti during the Pliocene to Pleistocene.
facts.quote: perfected by the Pliocene to Pleistocene Euthecodon brumpti

facts.statement: In Lothagam, Euthecodon brumpti coexisted with up to four different species of crocodiles.
facts.quote: In Lothagam, in the southwestern part of the Turkana Basin, Euthecodon brumpti coexisted with as many as four different species of crocodiles

facts.statement: Euthecodon and Eogavialis were heavily specialized for a piscivorous diet, preying on smaller fish.
facts.quote: Of these, Euthecodon and Eogavialis are heavily specialised for a piscivorous diet, specialising in preying on smaller fish

facts.statement: Moghara and Gebel Zelten preserve fluvio-marine environments with fossils of sharks, dolphins, sawfish, catfish, anthracotheres, carnivorans, proboscideans, and primates.
facts.quote: Both Moghara and Gebel Zelten preserve fluvio-marine environments yielding fossils of sharks, dolphins and sawfish alongside catfish, anthracotheres, carnivorans, proboscideans and primates

facts.statement: Gebel Zelten's environment is reconstructed as rivers banked by tropical forests feeding into a large lagoon, with intermediate areas covered by savanna.
facts.quote: Gebel Zelten is especially well understood, the environment being reconstructed as rivers banked by tropical forests coming from the south and feeding into a large lagoon, while the intermediate areas are covered by savanna

facts.statement: Euthecodon's specialized lifestyle may have prevented it from venturing into saltwater, restricting it to riverbanks further upstream.
facts.quote: This may be connected to its specialised lifestyle, preventing it from venturing too far out into saltwater and restricting it to the riverbanks further up river

facts.statement: Increased aridification, salinity, and conditions favoring temporary water bodies may have contributed to the disappearance of the highly specialized Euthecodon.
facts.quote: Eventually, increased aridification, increased salinity and conditions favoring more temporary bodies of water may have all contributed to the disappearance of the highly specialised Euthecodon

facts.statement: The genus Euthecodon was named by Fortau in 1920.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Euthecodon (genus), Fortau 1920

facts.statement: Euthecodon belongs to the subfamily Euthecodontini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Euthecodontini

facts.statement: Euthecodon is classified within the family Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: Family: Crocodylidae

facts.statement: Euthecodon is a member of the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Euthecodon is Euthecodon nitriae.
facts.quote: Type species: Euthecodon nitriae

facts.statement: Euthecodon lived from the Aquitanian to the Late Pleistocene, between 23.04 and 0.0117 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Late Pleistocene (23.04 to 0.0117 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 57 recorded fossil occurrences of Euthecodon.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 57
